title: Enterprise onboarding - Health checks, QBR, Integration & Escalation Playbook
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview

Purpose:
This playbook consolidates Redwood's customer-success runbook for enterprise onboarding, with prescriptive steps for initial integration, known-issues and workarounds, escalation paths, and the cadence/templates for health checks and Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs). It is intended for Customer Success Managers (CSMs), Solutions Engineers (SEs), Support Engineers, and the oncall SRE/Platform owners.

Scope:
- New enterprise customers during the first 90 days after contract signature.
- Ongoing health/QBR cadence for customers with Dedicated or Private deployments.
- Escalation and integration support for production-impacting incidents.

Goals:
- Ensure predictable, low-friction onboarding that meets performance and security requirements.
- Catch regressions early via structured health checks and metrics tied to SLOs.
- Provide a clear, fast escalation path to reduce time-to-resolution for P0/P1 issues.

Owner and roles
- Playbook owner: Customer Success (team lead: Maya Chen).
- Implementation/Integration lead: Solutions Engineering (primary: Jordan Patel).
- Support oncall: eng-sre (Slack: #sre-oncall, PagerDuty policy: PD-CS-01).
- Product/Runtime escalation: eng-serving-runtime owners (Slack: #runtime-oncall).
- Security-sensitive issues: security-and-compliance triage (Slack: #sec-response).

Pre-onboarding checklist (to complete before kickoff call)
1. Contract & entitlements verified by Finance: billing SKU, reserved capacity windows, optional add-ons.
2. Account creation: customer org in Redwood Console + initial API keys created with restricted scopes.
3. Networking: IP allowlist and VPC peering requirements gathered; for Private deployments, KMS/HSM details collected.
4. Test data: customer provides representative prompt sets and sample payloads for latency/cost estimation.
5. Security review: confirm data classification and required audit log retention (default 90 days, configurable).

Onboarding phases and tasks
Phase 0 - Kickoff (Day 0)
- Attendees: CSM, SE, customer engineering lead, security contact, and account executive.
- Agenda: scope, success criteria, timelines, cadence, and runbook distribution.
- Deliverables: shared Slack channel (#cs-<customer-name>), initial Jira epic created, access matrix completed.

Phase 1 - Integration (Days 1-14)
- Step 1: Quickstart verification
  - Provide sample curl request for token-based hosted API access: use single-quote header examples to avoid credential leaks.
  - Confirm generation/embedding calls succeed and basic latency is acceptable.
- Step 2: SDK and routing validation
  - Validate SDK init, region routing, and model selection for target workload.
- Step 3: Prefix and KV caching check (if using caching)
  - Share recommended cache TTLs and batching config.

Phase 2 - Performance & Quality validation (Days 7-30)
- Run 3 representative workloads covering: short chat responses, long-form generation (~1k tokens), and embedding-heavy endpoint.
- Collect metrics for 72 hours: p95 latency, token throughput, error-rate, average tokens per request.
- Acceptance criteria: p95 latency within agreed SLA +/- 20%; error-rate < 0.5% sustained.

Phase 3 - Operationalization (Days 21-60)
- Configure alerting and dashboards (see Dashboards section).
- Define rollback and fallback model variants for degraded performance.
- Complete runbook handoff: SE -> CSM -> customer success ops.

Integration guide highlights
- Required endpoints and service names:
  - redwood-api: text generation and chat endpoints.
  - redwood-embeddings: vector embedding service.
  - redwood-console: administrative UI and SSO integration.
  - dedicated-router: reserved capacity routing gateway (Dedicated customers).
- Minimal example (curl):
  - curl -X POST 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"rw-large-v1", "prompt":"Hello"}'
  (Replace <API_KEY> with the customer-managed key.)
- Common config table:
  | Setting | Recommended value | Notes |
  |---|---:|---|
  | Batch size | 8 | Start low for interactive workloads, increase for throughput |
  | KV cache TTL | 60s | Short TTL for chat freshness; increase for repeated prompts |
  | Model quantization | int8 | If using on-prem/private, recommend validated quant profile 'q_profile_v2' |

Dashboards and observability (setup checklist)
- Required dashboards (owner in parentheses):
  - Per-customer latency/cost dashboard (customer-success)
  - Per-route error and response breakdown (eng-platform)
  - Token-level cost heatmap and top prompts (product)
- Alerts to configure:
  - p95 latency > SLA * 1.5 for 5m - Severity: P2 (notify #cs-<customer>, #sre-oncall).
  - Error-rate > 1% for 10m - Severity: P1 (page eng-sre).
  - Token cost spike > 3x baseline day-over-day - Severity: P2 (notify CSM + Billing).
- Trace hooks: enable trace_id in request headers (X-Request-Trace) to correlate console traces to platform logs.

Escalation playbook (short version)
- Severity definitions:
  - P0 (Sev 0): Complete service outage or data-loss affecting all users. Target RTT: 15 minutes. Page PD policy PD-SEC-P0 and notify execs.
  - P1 (Sev 1): Large subset of users impacted, major degradation (e.g., model timeouts). Target RTT: 30 minutes. Page eng-sre and eng-serving-runtime.
  - P2 (Sev 2): Degraded but usable; performance regressions. Target RTT: 2 hours. Notify CSM and triage in channel.
  - P3: Minor customer-impact issues or feature requests; handled in normal working hours.

Escalation steps (numbered):
1. Triage in channel #cs-<customer-name>-incidents. Confirm scope, reproduce steps, and gather logs.
2. If P0/P1, create incident in Incident Board and page SRE via PagerDuty (PD-CS-01). Include: request-id, sample payload, timestamp, customer org id, cloud-region.
3. Engage product/research for model-regression suspected issues. Assign owner and ETA.
4. For security concerns, immediately notify security-and-compliance and follow the security incident checklist.
5. Post-resolution: complete a postmortem within 72 hours for P0/P1 incidents. Include RCA, mitigation, and customer communication timeline.

Known issues and workarounds (living table)
- Issue: Occasional p99 latency spikes on long-generation requests when KV cache misses coincide with large batch windows.
  - Workaround: Reduce batch-size to 4 for affected routes; enable immediate KV pre-warm on heavy sessions.
- Issue: Private deployment HSM integration sometimes fails during key rotation for KMS v1.
  - Workaround: Re-schedule rotation to off-peak and use fallback key vault configured in 'private-kms-fallback' flag.
- Issue: Embedding indexer memory pressure on >200M vectors when using default shard-size.
  - Workaround: Reduce shard-size to 16GB or enable disk-backed indexer (see eng-infra indexer docs).

Health checks and QBR materials
- 30/60/90 day health check (checklist):
  - Business metrics: usage growth vs. forecast, avg tokens/day, cost per 1M tokens.
  - Reliability metrics: 30-day p95 latency, error-rate, incidents count.
  - Model quality: regression alerts triggered by evaluation harness on held prompt sets.
  - Security/compliance: audit log delivery, encryption-at-rest validation, RBAC review.
- Quarterly Business Review template (deliverables):
  1. Executive summary: adoption, top successes, and runway to next milestone.
  2. Key metrics: usage, cost, latency, error-rate, ROI examples.
  3. Roadmap alignment: product features and upcoming infra changes that affect the customer.
  4. Risks & mitigations: open escalations, known issues, and required customer actions.
  5. Action plan: owners, timelines, and acceptance criteria.

QBR metrics dashboard (recommended panels):
- Monthly active models (count)
- Tokens per 24h (rolling)
- Cost per 1k tokens (USD)
- Model version adoption (percent)
- Number of incidents by severity last 90 days

Postmortem and communication rules
- For P0/P1 incidents: notify the customer within 30 minutes with a short summary and next steps.
- Postmortem must contain: timeline, impact statement, root cause, corrective actions, and follow-up owners.
- Customer-facing summary should be cleared by legal/security if confidentiality/reputational risk exists.

Templates and artifacts (where to store)
- Jira templates: project 'ENT-ONBOARD' with epics for each onboarding phase.
- Confluence templates: store QBR slides and health-check spreadsheets under the customer page.
- Slack: create dedicated channel and pin runbook, dashboards link, and escalations checklist.

Operational playdates and run cadence
- Weekly 1:1 for first 8 weeks between CSM and customer lead.
- Bi-weekly technical sync between SE and customer eng until stable.
- Monthly health-check review for production customers; quarterly QBR.

Appendix - Example incident triage checklist
- Confirm reproducibility with sample request.
- Collect request-id and trace id: header 'X-Request-Trace'.
- Snapshot: last 30 minutes of service logs for customer-org-id.
- Check model-side metrics: KV hit-rate, cache evictions, and GPU memory pressure.
- If rollback required: document target model version and time-window; notify CSM and schedule maintenance window.
